question: True or false: a line showing a firm's total sales since launch can rise every quarter while its sales shrink?
answer: True. A running total adds each quarter's sales to all the earlier ones, so it can only climb or stay flat. Quarterly sales of 10, 8, 6 and 4 million give totals of 10, 18, 24 and 28 million: a line climbing steadily while sales drop by a fifth or more each quarter.
move: A running total only goes up; ask for each period on its own.
ask: When a company shows me a line that always rises, do I ask to see each year on its own?
trap: False, because a rising line on a chart means a growing business.
source: Huff, How to Lie with Statistics
reference: Huff, How to Lie with Statistics, W. W. Norton, 1954
